author: HID production runtime applicability assessment
hid_scope: gateway image only; exact libssl3 and libcrypto3 3.5.9-r0 aarch64 Alpine 3.24.2 purls; original findings retained in grype.raw.json; no risk-acceptance waiver

statements.impact_statement: The affected AES-GCM-SIV incremental AAD update is in the libcrypto3 default provider and is reached only by fetching AES-GCM-SIV by name and feeding AAD in pieces; it is not a TLS cipher. nginx and njs import only the legacy EVP_aes_*_{cbc,ctr,gcm}, aes_128_ccm and chacha20(-poly1305) constructors, and neither imports EVP_CIPHER_fetch or EVP_get_cipherbyname. The gateway image (nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged@sha256:782bb897..., Alpine 3.24.2, arm64) serves through nginx 1.30.7-r1 (nginx.org Alpine 3.24 package, pinned in gateway/Dockerfile) with gateway/nginx.conf.template: one plain-HTTP listen 3000 with no ssl or quic parameter, and every proxy_pass target is an http:// *_UPSTREAM value, so nginx never creates a TLS or QUIC session. No load_module directive exists, so the njs, xslt, geoip and image-filter modules are never loaded. The only other OpenSSL user that runs is the entrypoint's apk manifest (libapk imports only digest, PEM key and TLS-client symbols); c_rehash is never run, and the wget health check is plain http://127.0.0.1:3000, so busybox's ssl_client is not started. Assessed 2026-11-18 from the base layers fetched by digest. Rechecked 2026-11-19 for nginx and modules 1.30.7-r1: the same OpenSSL imports as 1.30.6-r1, and no nginx, module or njs ELF imports EVP_CIPHER_fetch, EVP_get_cipherbyname, OSSL_QUIC_*, CMS_*, PEM_X509_INFO_* or SSL_new_listener. Alpine 3.24 serves no libssl3/libcrypto3 newer than 3.5.9-r0; OpenSSL 3.5.10 is due 2026-12-01. Expires 2026-12-01: replace with a pinned fixed Alpine 3.24 package, do not renew.
